Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver function tests, complete blood counts, and blood glucose levels, should be conducted as recommended by your healthcare provider. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is less than 8 hours before your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This document is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. To ensure optimal effectiveness, take this medication at least 4 hours before or 8 hours after consuming other products that may bind to it and reduce its efficacy. Consult your pharmacist about any other products you are taking. For the best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow bacteria to continue growing, potentially leading to a relapse of the infection. Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, weakness, or difficulty sleeping. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may also result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Before taking moxifloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (such as ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin), or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Moxifloxacin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, particularly if you have diabetes. Monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Be alert for symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination, as well as symptoms of low blood sugar, such as sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet. To treat low blood sugar, it is advisable to carry glucose tablets or gel. If these are unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming a fast source of sugar, such as table sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Inform your doctor immediately about any reactions and the use of this product. To prevent low blood sugar, eat meals on a regular schedule and avoid skipping meals. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Moxifloxacin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist.
